13. Why can the displayed value of a floating-point number differ slightly from the value written in the program?
Floating-point values are stored using a limited number of bits.
When more fractional digits are supplied than the representation can retain precisely, some digits may be rounded.
14. What is the purpose of character encoding?
Character encoding assigns a unique binary code to each character so that characters can be stored and retrieved without ambiguity.
If different characters used the same binary representation, the computer would not know which character the stored bits represent.
15. Why does the number of bits required for character encoding increase when the number of characters increases?
Every character requires a unique binary code.
As the number of characters increases, more binary combinations are required.

34. Why can ASCII characters be stored using one byte even though 128 values require only 7 bits?
Seven bits are sufficient to represent 128 different values, but one byte contains 8 bits.
Therefore, an additional bit can be added so that the character representation occupies one complete byte.
